properties.key: Stable identity used to preserve state across rebuilds.
properties.data: Arbitrary value you can attach to the control and read back in handlers.
properties.label: Text label shown for the control.
properties.content: The single child control rendered inside this control.
properties.title: The control shown as the title.
properties.subtitle: The control shown as the secondary line below the title.
properties.leading: Control placed before the main content (e.g. an icon or avatar).
properties.trailing: Control placed after the main content.
properties.actions: Controls shown in the trailing action area.
properties.icon: Icon name shown by the control.
properties.src: Source URL or asset path of the image.
properties.url: URL the control loads or links to.
properties.options: The selectable options (built with the control's option helper).
properties.divisions: Number of discrete steps between min and max.
properties.hint_text: Placeholder shown when the field is empty.
properties.helper_text: Helper text shown below the field.
properties.error_text: Error message shown below the field; also marks it invalid.
properties.password: Obscures the entered text when true.
properties.multiline: Allows multiple lines of input when true.
properties.read_only: Prevents editing while still allowing selection.
properties.clip_behavior: How content overflowing the bounds is clipped.
properties.expand: Fills the available space along the parent's main axis when true.
properties.expand_loose: Like expand, but only grows up to the child's natural size.
properties.padding: Inner spacing between the border and the content.
properties.align: Alignment of the control within its parent.
properties.alignment: Alignment of the content within the control.
properties.top: Top offset when positioned inside a stack.
properties.bottom: Bottom offset when positioned inside a stack.
properties.left: Left offset when positioned inside a stack.
properties.right: Right offset when positioned inside a stack.
properties.scale: Scale transform applied to the control.
properties.offset: Translation offset applied to the control.
properties.adaptive: Adapts to the platform (Material/Cupertino) when true.
properties.badge: Badge drawn on the corner of the control.
properties.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown when hovering the control.
properties.size_change_interval: Throttle interval for on_size_change, in ms.
properties.action: A client action, built with `Ruflet.client_action`, that the client runs inside the tap before it sends `on_click`. Use it for work browsers allow only during a user gesture, such as opening a link, copying to the clipboard or picking files.
properties.spacing: Space between the control's children, or between its parts such as a checkbox and its label, in logical pixels.
properties.run_spacing: Space between lines of children when they wrap, in logical pixels.
properties.tight: Takes only as much space along the main axis as the children need.
properties.reverse: Reverses the direction: lists start from the end, and animations play backwards.
properties.horizontal: Lays the items out and scrolls them horizontally instead of vertically.
properties.scroll: Makes the content scrollable when it overflows: `"auto"`, `"adaptive"`, `"always"` or `"hidden"` (no scrollbar).
properties.scroll_interval: Minimum time between `on_scroll` events, in milliseconds (default 10).
properties.auto_scroll: Scrolls to the end automatically whenever the children change, as in a chat or log view.
properties.auto_scroll_animation: How `auto_scroll` moves to the end: a duration in milliseconds, `{ duration:, curve: }`, or `false` to jump.
properties.keyboard_dismiss_behavior: Whether scrolling closes the on-screen keyboard: `"manual"` (default) or `"onDrag"`.
properties.end_reached_threshold: How close to the end, in logical pixels, the user must scroll before `on_end_reached` fires (default 200).
properties.item_extent: Size of each item along the scroll direction, in logical pixels, such as the row height of a picker wheel.
properties.cache_extent: How far beyond the visible area, in logical pixels, the list builds items ahead of time.
properties.build_controls_on_demand: Builds only the children that are scrolled into view (default `true`).
properties.semantic_child_count: Number of items screen readers announce for the list.
properties.divider_thickness: Thickness of the dividers drawn between items or rows, in logical pixels.
properties.first_item_prototype: Uses the first item to measure the size of every item, which speeds up layout.
properties.prototype_item: A sample item used to measure the size of every item.
properties.show_default_drag_handles: Shows the platform drag handle on each item; set `false` to drag only by your own `reorderable_drag_handle`.
properties.auto_scroller_velocity_scalar: How fast the list scrolls while an item is dragged near its edge.
properties.anchor: Relative position, from 0.0 to 1.0, of the zero scroll offset in the viewport.
properties.selected_index: Index of the selected item, starting at 0.
properties.size: Size of the control: a number in logical pixels for icons, text and indicators, or a size name such as `"small"` or `"large"` for buttons.
properties.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button.
properties.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the control fades to while it is pressed.
properties.icon_size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels.
properties.gradient: Gradient that fills the control instead of a solid color.
properties.blend_mode: How the control's color or shader is combined with what is behind it, for example `"multiply"` or `"srcIn"`.
properties.border_side: Border line, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`.
properties.fit: How the content is sized into the available space: a box fit such as `"contain"` or `"cover"` for images and animations, a stack fit such as `"expand"` for stacks.
properties.repeat: Repeats the content: loops an animation, or tiles an image (`"repeat"`, `"repeatX"`, `"repeatY"`).
properties.x: Horizontal position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the x axis in a chart.
properties.y: Vertical position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the y axis in a chart.
properties.paint: How a canvas shape is drawn (color, stroke width, fill or stroke, gradient), built with `paint(...)`.
properties.semantics_label: Text that screen readers announce for the control.
properties.semantics_value: Value that screen readers announce, such as a progress percentage.
properties.exclude_from_semantics: Hides the control from screen readers; on a gesture detector, hides its gestures.
properties.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space.
properties.direction: Layout direction of the segments: `"horizontal"` (default) or `"vertical"`.
properties.variant: Style variant of the control, for example `"elevated"`, `"filled"` or `"outlined"` for a card.
properties.label_position: Side of the control the label is placed on: `"right"` (default) or `"left"`.
properties.toggleable: Lets a second tap clear the selection.
properties.default: Marks the action as the default one; iOS shows it in bold.
properties.destructive: Marks the action as destructive; iOS shows it in red.
properties.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog or sheet does not close it.
properties.scrollable: Lets the content scroll when it does not fit.
properties.maintain_state: Keeps the hidden children alive while the control is collapsed.
properties.extended: Shows each label beside its icon instead of under it.
properties.label_type: Which destination labels are shown: `"all"`, `"selected"` or `"none"`.
properties.group_alignment: How the groups of items are aligned.
properties.use_indicator: Draws a highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.indicator_shape: Shape of the highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.min_width: Minimum width of the control, in logical pixels.
properties.min_extended_width: Width of the rail when `extended` is true.
properties.duration: Length of the control's animation, or how long it stays visible, in milliseconds.
properties.reverse_duration: Length of the animation for the outgoing content, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_duration: Length of the control's transition animation, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_curve: Easing curve of the control's transition animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.switch_in_curve: Easing curve for the incoming content, for example `"easeOut"`.
properties.switch_out_curve: Easing curve for the outgoing content, for example `"easeIn"`.
properties.transition: Animation between the old and the new content: `"fade"` (default), `"scale"` or `"rotation"`.
properties.animating: Runs the animation while true; set `false` to pause it.
properties.animation: Animation applied when the chart data changes: a duration in milliseconds or `{ duration:, curve: }`.
properties.begin: Value the transition animation starts from.
properties.end: Value the transition animation ends at.
properties.curve: Easing curve of the animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.delay: Time to wait before the animation starts, in milliseconds.
properties.sliding: Selects the sliding iOS segmented control; set by `cupertino_sliding_segmented_button`.
properties.interval: Time between sensor readings, in milliseconds.
properties.enabled: Turns the sensor stream on or off.
properties.cancel_on_error: Stops the sensor stream after the first error.
properties.interactive: Enables touch tooltips and highlights on the chart (default `true`).
properties.min_x: Smallest value shown on the x axis.
properties.max_x: Largest value shown on the x axis.
properties.min_y: Smallest value shown on the y axis.
properties.max_y: Largest value shown on the y axis.
properties.left_axis: Axis drawn on the left of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.right_axis: Axis drawn on the right of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.top_axis: Axis drawn above the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.bottom_axis: Axis drawn below the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.show_tooltip: Shows the tooltip for this data point.
properties.capitalization: Automatic capitalization of typed text: `"none"`, `"words"`, `"sentences"` or `"characters"`.
properties.text_align: Horizontal alignment of the text: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, `"start"` or `"end"`.
properties.text_size: Font size of the typed text.
properties.text_vertical_align: Vertical position of the text in a tall field, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).
properties.error: Error shown below the field, as text or a control; it also marks the field invalid.
properties.helper: Helper text or control shown below the field.
properties.counter: Text or control shown below the field on the right, often a character count.
properties.prefix: Text or control shown inside the field before the input.
properties.suffix: Text or control shown inside the field after the input.
properties.collapsed: Removes the field's decoration and padding for a minimal input.
properties.align_label_with_hint: Aligns the label with the hint text; useful for multiline fields.
properties.fit_parent_size: Makes the field fill its parent's size.
properties.hint_fade_duration: Time the hint takes to fade when the user starts typing, in milliseconds.
properties.error_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of error text.
properties.helper_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of helper text.
properties.hint_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of hint text.
properties.max_length: Maximum number of characters the user can enter; a counter shows the count.
properties.max_lines: Maximum number of lines the control shows.
properties.min_lines: Minimum number of lines the field shows.
properties.input_filter: Limits which characters can be typed, with a regular expression.
properties.autofill_hints: Hints for the platform's autofill, for example `["email"]`.
properties.can_reveal_password: Shows an eye button that reveals a `password` field's text.
properties.obscuring_character: Character shown in place of each typed character in a `password` field.
properties.shift_enter: In a multiline field, Enter submits and Shift+Enter starts a new line.
properties.can_request_focus: Whether the field can take keyboard focus.
properties.always_call_on_tap: Fires `on_click` on every tap, even when the field already has focus.
properties.enable_interactive_selection: Lets the user select text and use copy and paste.
properties.enable_ime_personalized_learning: Lets the keyboard learn from what the user types.
properties.enable_stylus_handwriting: Allows handwriting input with a stylus where the platform supports it.
properties.ignore_up_down_keys: Ignores the up and down arrow keys in the field.
properties.keyboard_brightness: Appearance of the iOS keyboard: `"light"` or `"dark"`.
properties.smart_dashes_type: Turns iOS smart dashes on or off.
properties.smart_quotes_type: Turns iOS smart quotes on or off.
properties.shadows: Drop shadows painted behind the control.
properties.text_input_action: The keyboard's action button, such as `"next"`, `"search"` or `"done"`.
properties.placeholder_text: Prompt shown while the field is empty (Cupertino look only; `hint_text` takes precedence).
properties.clear_button_visibility_mode: When the clear button shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`.
properties.clear_button_semantics_label: Label screen readers announce for the clear button.
properties.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`.
properties.first_date: Earliest date the user can pick.
properties.last_date: Latest date the user can pick.
properties.entry_mode: How the value is entered, for example `"calendar"` or `"input"` for dates and `"dial"` or `"input"` for times.
properties.minute_interval: Step between selectable minutes, for example 5.
properties.allow_multiple_selection: Lets more than one segment be selected.
properties.allow_empty_selection: Lets the user clear the selection.
properties.round: Number of decimal places shown in the value label.
properties.suggestions: The suggestions the user can pick from.
properties.suggestions_max_height: Maximum height of the suggestion list, in logical pixels.
properties.menu_position: Where the menu opens relative to the button: `"over"` or `"under"`.
properties.foreground_image_src: Image drawn over the avatar's content, usually the user's photo.
properties.background_image_src: Image drawn behind the avatar's content.
properties.background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from start to end (right, or down); also used for the other direction when `secondary_background` is not set.
properties.secondary_background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from end to start (left, or up).
properties.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the control: `"horizontal"`, `"endToStart"`, `"startToEnd"`, `"vertical"`, `"up"`, `"down"` or `"none"`.
properties.dismiss_thresholds: Fraction of the width or height the control must travel before it is dismissed, per direction.
properties.movement_duration: Time the control takes to slide away or back, in milliseconds (default 200).
properties.resize_duration: Time the space left by a dismissed control takes to close, in milliseconds (default 300).
properties.cross_axis_end_offset: Moves the control across the swipe direction, as a fraction of its size, as it is dismissed.
properties.drag_interval: Minimum time between drag update events, in milliseconds.
properties.hover_interval: Minimum time between hover events, in milliseconds.
properties.multi_tap_touches: Number of fingers that `on_multi_tap` waits for.
properties.allowed_devices: Pointer kinds that can start a gesture, for example `["touch", "mouse"]`.
properties.trackpad_scroll_causes_scale: Treats two-finger trackpad scrolling as a pinch.
properties.sort_column_index: Index of the column that shows the sort arrow.
properties.sort_ascending: Direction of the sort arrow: `true` for ascending.
properties.show_checkbox_column: Adds a checkbox column for selecting rows.
properties.show_bottom_border: Draws a border below the last row.
properties.column_spacing: Space between columns, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_margin: Space before the first and after the last column, in logical pixels.
properties.checkbox_horizontal_margin: Space around the row checkboxes, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_lines: Border line between rows, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_lines: Border line between columns, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.data_row_min_height: Minimum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.data_row_max_height: Maximum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.heading_row_height: Height of the heading row, in logical pixels.
properties.viewport_fraction: Share of the viewport each page fills; below 1.0 the neighbouring pages show at the edges.
properties.pad_ends: Adds space before the first and after the last page when `viewport_fraction` is below 1.0.
properties.snap: Snaps to a resting position, such as a whole page, when the user stops dragging.
properties.keep_page: Restores the current page when the page view is rebuilt.
properties.implicit_scrolling: Lets assistive technology move to the next and previous page.
properties.force_actions_below: Puts the actions under the message instead of beside it.
properties.notch_margin: Space between the floating action button and the notch, in logical pixels.
properties.full_screen: Opens the search view full screen.
properties.shrink_wrap: Sizes the control to its content instead of filling the available space.
properties.bar_elevation: Shadow depth of the search bar.
properties.bar_leading: Control shown at the start of the search bar.
properties.bar_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search bar.
properties.bar_size_constraints: Size limits of the search bar.
properties.view_elevation: Shadow depth of the search view.
properties.view_leading: Control shown at the start of the search view's header.
properties.view_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search view's header.
properties.view_size_constraints: Size limits of the search view.
properties.year_2023: Uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
properties.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the track, in logical pixels.
properties.affinity: Where the expand icon sits: `"leading"`, `"trailing"` or `"platform"`.
properties.collapsed_shape: Shape of the tile while collapsed.
properties.unit_id: Your AdMob ad unit ID; without it the client loads Google's test ad unit.
properties.request: Targeting options for the ad request, such as keywords.
properties.active_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is on.
properties.inactive_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is off.
properties.item_count: Number of items in the indicator, for variants that draw several.
properties.wave_type: Where the wave starts for wave variants: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
properties.horizontal_grid_lines: Horizontal grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 10, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_grid_lines: Vertical grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 1, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.baseline_x: x value the chart draws from.
properties.baseline_y: y value the chart draws from, such as the bottom of the bars.
properties.coordinates: Position on the map as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`; a list of positions for lines and shapes.
properties.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40).
properties.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull on iOS to start a refresh.
properties.refresh_timeout: Longest time, in milliseconds, the refresh indicator waits for `on_refresh` (default 30 seconds).
properties.enable_alpha: Lets the user pick a transparency value as well as a color.
properties.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the prefix icon.
properties.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the suffix icon.
properties.show_drag_handle: Shows a drag handle at the top of the sheet.
properties.automatically_imply_leading: Adds a back or menu button automatically when the page has somewhere to go back to or a drawer.
properties.transition_between_routes: Animates the bar between pages on iOS.
properties.previous_page_title: Title of the previous page, shown next to the iOS back button.
properties.message: Smaller text below the title, as a string or a control.
properties.cancel: An `action_sheet_action` set apart below the other actions, for closing the sheet without choosing one.
properties.application_name: Name of the app, shown as the dialog title. Without it the dialog uses the app's window title.
properties.application_version: Version shown next to the app name, for example `"2.1.0"`.
properties.application_legalese: Small print shown in the dialog and on the licenses page, such as a copyright notice.
properties.application_icon: Control shown as the app's icon, usually an `icon` or an `image`.
properties.view: `"about"` (default) opens the about dialog; `"licenses"` opens the open-source licenses page directly, as a full page instead of a dialog.
properties.bar_height: Thickness of the bar, in logical pixels (default 4; 3 on iOS and macOS).
properties.stop_indicator_color: Color of the dot at the end of the track. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
properties.stop_indicator_radius: Radius of the dot at the end of the track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
properties.placeholder: A control shown in place of the content while it loads.
properties.show_edit_icon: Shows a pencil icon in the cell to tell users they can edit it; handle the cell's `on_tap` to start editing.
properties.cells: The `data_cell` controls of the row, one per column; the first positional argument sets them.
properties.heading_row_alignment: How the heading is aligned in its cell: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
properties.fixed_width: Fixed width of the column, in logical pixels; it replaces the `size` share.
properties.specific_row_height: Height of this row, in logical pixels, instead of the table's `data_row_height`.
properties.data_row_height: Height of every data row, in logical pixels.
properties.bottom_margin: Space below the last row, in logical pixels (default 0).
properties.empty: Control shown in place of the rows while the table has none.
properties.fixed_left_columns: Number of columns at the start that stay in place while the table scrolls sideways (default 0).
properties.fixed_top_rows: Number of rows at the top, the heading row included, that stay in place while the table scrolls (default 1).
properties.fixed_columns_color: Background color of the fixed columns.
properties.fixed_corner_color: Background color of the corner where the fixed rows and fixed columns meet.
properties.lm_ratio: Width of an `"l"` column relative to an `"m"` column (default 1.2).
properties.sm_ratio: Width of an `"s"` column relative to an `"m"` column (default 0.67).
properties.heading_row_decoration: Box decoration of the heading row, for example `{ bgcolor: "#f1f5f9", border_radius: 8 }`.
properties.heading_checkbox_theme: Checkbox theme of the heading checkbox: `{ fill_color:, check_color:, border_side:, shape: }`.
properties.data_row_checkbox_theme: Checkbox theme of the row checkboxes: `{ fill_color:, check_color:, border_side:, shape: }`.
properties.show_heading_checkbox: Shows the select-all checkbox in the heading row while `show_checkbox_column` is on (default true).
properties.checkbox_alignment: Alignment of the checkboxes in their column, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0 (centered by default).
properties.sort_arrow_animation_duration: Length of the sort arrow's turn animation, in milliseconds.
properties.sort_arrow_icon: Icon used for the sort arrow (default `"arrow_upward"`).
properties.visible_horizontal_scroll_bar: Keeps the horizontal scroll bar visible while the table can scroll sideways.
properties.visible_vertical_scroll_bar: Keeps the vertical scroll bar visible while the table can scroll up and down.
properties.can_tap_header: Lets a tap anywhere on the header toggle the panel, not only on the arrow button (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it: the whole header always toggles the panel there.
properties.additional_divider_margin: Extra inset of the dividers on top of `divider_margin`, so they start after leading icons (default 56 on Android, web, Windows and Linux and 44 on iOS and macOS when `has_leading` is true, 0 otherwise).
properties.divider_margin: Inset of the dividers between rows from the section's leading edge, in logical pixels (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 20 on iOS and macOS).
properties.has_leading: Tells the section that its rows have leading icons, so the dividers start after them (default true).
properties.top_margin: Extra space above the section, in logical pixels (default 0; 22 on iOS and macOS for the `"base"` variant).
properties.separator_color: Color of the dividers between rows.
properties.column_widths: Widths per column index: `{ 0 => { type: "flex", value: 2 } }`, where `type` is `"flex"`, `"fixed"`, `"fraction"` or `"intrinsic"`; a bare number is a fixed width.
properties.default_column_width: Width of the columns missing from `column_widths`, in the same form (default: equal flex shares).
properties.inner_borders: Also draws lines between the rows and columns when `border_color` is set (default true).
properties.default_vertical_alignment: Vertical position of the cells in their row: `"top"` (default), `"middle"`, `"bottom"`, `"baseline"` or `"fill"`.

events.on_click: Fired when the control is clicked/tapped.
events.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts changing the value.
events.on_change_end: Fired when the user finishes changing the value.
events.on_submit: Fired when the input is submitted.
events.on_focus: Fired when the control gains focus.
events.on_blur: Fired when the control loses focus.
events.on_hover: Fired when the pointer enters/leaves the control.
events.on_tap_down: Fired when a pointer presses down.
events.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap is cancelled.
events.on_tap_outside: Fired when a tap occurs outside the control.
events.on_dismiss: Fired when the control is dismissed.
events.on_scroll: Fired when the scroll position changes.
events.on_select: Fired when a selection is made.
events.on_selection_change: Fired when the selection range changes.
events.on_state_change: Fired when the control's state changes.
events.on_enter: Fired when the pointer enters the control.
events.on_exit: Fired when the pointer leaves the control.
events.on_image_error: Fired when the image fails to load.
events.on_loaded: Fired when the control has loaded.
events.on_visible: Fired when the control appears on screen.
events.on_resize: Fired when the control is resized.
events.on_size_change: Fired when the control's size changes.
events.on_action_result: Fired when a client `action:` has finished; the event carries its result or error.
events.on_end_reached: Fired when the user scrolls near the end, for loading more items.
events.on_refresh: Fired when the user pulls down to refresh; the indicator spins until the handler returns.
events.on_paste_files: Fired when the user pastes files into the field; `event.files` lists them.
events.on_tap_outside_view: Fired when the user taps outside the open search view.
events.on_tap_outside_bar: Fired when the user taps outside the search bar.
events.on_reading: Fired with each new sensor reading in `event.data`.
events.on_event: Fired on chart or map touch and pointer events; `event.data` describes the event.
events.on_load: Fired when the content has loaded.
events.on_cancel: Fired when the menu closes without a choice.
events.on_impression: Fired when the ad is shown to the user.
events.on_will_dismiss: Fired just before a screen the ad opened closes.
events.on_paid: Fired when the ad earns revenue; `event.data` holds the value and currency.
events.on_reorder: Fired when an item is dropped in a new position; `event.old_index` and `event.new_index` give the move.
events.on_reorder_start: Fired when the user starts dragging an item.
events.on_reorder_end: Fired when the user drops a dragged item.
events.on_confirm_dismiss: Fired before the control is dismissed. Reply with `page.invoke(event.control, "confirm_dismiss", args: { dismiss: true })`, or `dismiss: false` to keep it; without a reply the client cancels the dismissal after five minutes.
events.on_update: Fired while the control is dragged, with the direction and progress.
events.on_select_all: Fired when the user taps the select-all checkbox in the heading row; `event.data` is `true` to select every row and `nil` to clear them. Without this handler the table calls each row's `on_select_change` instead.
events.on_select_change: Fired when the user selects or clears the row; `event.data` is `true` when it is selected and `nil` when it is cleared. The row does not change by itself: set its `selected` with `page.update`.
events.on_sort: Fired when the user taps the column heading to sort; `event.data[:ci]` is the column index and `event.data[:asc]` the new direction.
events.on_tap_up: Fired when a pointer that pressed down lifts.
events.on_pan_start: Fired when a drag in any direction starts.
events.on_pan_update: Fired as a drag moves; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update.
events.on_pan_end: Fired when a drag ends; the event carries the velocity.
events.on_horizontal_drag_start: Fired when a horizontal drag starts.
events.on_horizontal_drag_update: Fired as a horizontal drag moves.
events.on_horizontal_drag_end: Fired when a horizontal drag ends.
events.on_vertical_drag_start: Fired when a vertical drag starts.
events.on_vertical_drag_update: Fired as a vertical drag moves.
events.on_vertical_drag_end: Fired when a vertical drag ends.
events.on_scale_start: Fired when a pinch or two-finger rotation starts.

expansiontile.maintain_state: Keeps the hidden controls alive while the tile is closed (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it and remove them.
expansiontile.affinity: Where the arrow icon sits: `"leading"`, `"trailing"` or `"platform"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.animation_style: Duration and curves of the open and close animation: `{ duration:, reverse_duration:, curve:, reverse_curve: }`, with durations in milliseconds. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.clip_behavior: How the tile clips its content. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.icon_color: Color of the arrow icon while the tile is open. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.collapsed_icon_color: Color of the arrow icon while the tile is closed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.text_color: Color of the title while the tile is open. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.collapsed_text_color: Color of the title while the tile is closed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.shape: Border shape of the tile while it is open. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.collapsed_shape: Border shape of the tile while it is closed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.dense: Uses a more compact header. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's tap sound and haptic feedback when the header is tapped. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.expanded_alignment: Alignment of the revealed controls, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.expanded_cross_axis_alignment: Horizontal alignment of the revealed controls: `"center"` (default), `"start"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.min_tile_height: Minimum height of the header row, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.visual_density: Compactness of the header: `"standard"`, `"compact"`, `"comfortable"` or `"adaptivePlatformDensity"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
expansiontile.on_change: Fired when the user opens or closes the tile; `event.data` is `true` when it opens and `nil` when it closes.

formrow.prefix: Label or control shown at the start of the row.
formrow.helper: Text or control shown below the row.
formrow.error: Error text or control shown below the row.

listsection.controls: The rows of the section; the first positional argument, `children:` or a block sets them.
listsection.variant: `"insetGrouped"` (default): rounded rows inset from the screen edges; `"base"`: rows from edge to edge.
listsection.border_radius: Corner radius of the rows' background (default 12 on Android, web, Windows and Linux and 10 on iOS and macOS for `"insetGrouped"`, square for `"base"`).
listsection.margin: Space around the section (by default 16 at the sides and 8 above and below for `"insetGrouped"` on Android, web, Windows and Linux).

listtile.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.hover_color: Color of the tile while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.is_three_line: Gives the subtitle room for two lines, so the tile is three lines tall. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.shape: Shape of the tile's background and tap highlight. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.title: Main text of the row, as a string or a control; required.
listtile.subtitle: Secondary text below the title, as a string or a control.
listtile.url: Opens this URL in the browser when the row is tapped.
listtile.chevron: Adds a chevron after `trailing` to show that the row opens something (default false).
listtile.toggle_inputs: Makes a tap anywhere on the row toggle the `switch`, `checkbox` or `radio` inside it (default false).
listtile.content_padding: Padding inside the row, around its content.
listtile.padding: The `cupertino_list_tile` spelling of `content_padding`: padding inside the row.
listtile.selected: Draws the row in its selected colors on Android, web, Windows and Linux. On iOS and macOS it only tells screen readers that the row is selected.
listtile.additional_info: Detail text shown before `trailing`, like the value on the right of an iOS Settings row, as a string or a control. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
listtile.bgcolor_activated: Background color while the row is pressed on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
listtile.leading_size: Size of the box `leading` is drawn in on iOS and macOS (default 28, or 30 when `notched`). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
listtile.leading_to_title: Gap between `leading` and the title on iOS and macOS (default 16, or 12 when `notched`). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
listtile.notched: Uses the iOS inset-grouped row style, with a larger leading area (default false). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
listtile.autofocus: Gives the row keyboard focus when it first appears. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.horizontal_spacing: Gap between `leading` and the title, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.min_leading_width: Minimum width of the leading area, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.min_vertical_padding: Minimum padding above and below the content, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.min_height: Minimum height of the row, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.visual_density: Compactness of the row: `"standard"`, `"compact"`, `"comfortable"` or `"adaptivePlatformDensity"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.style: Which text sizes the row uses: `"list"` (default) or `"drawer"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.title_alignment: Vertical position of `leading` and `trailing` next to the text: `"threeLine"`, `"titleHeight"`, `"top"`, `"center"` or `"bottom"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.icon_color: Color of the leading and trailing icons. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.text_color: Color of the title, subtitle, leading and trailing text. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.selected_color: Color of the text and icons while `selected`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.selected_tile_color: Background color while `selected`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.focus_color: Background color while the row has keyboard focus. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.splash_color: Color of the ink ripple when the row is tapped. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's tap sound and haptic feedback when the row is tapped. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown while the pointer is over the row. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.title_text_style: Text style of a string title. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.subtitle_text_style: Text style of a string subtitle. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.leading_and_trailing_text_style: Text style of string leading and trailing text. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.on_click: Fired when the user taps the row.
listtile.on_long_press: Fired when the user long-presses the row.

navigationrail.group_alignment: Vertical position of the destinations, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).

popupmenubutton.on_select: Fired when an item is chosen; the data is the item's internal id, so handle each item's `on_click` instead.

progressbar.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for an indeterminate bar.
progressbar.bgcolor: Color of the track behind the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system's light gray.
progressbar.color: Color of the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system blue.
progressbar.track_gap: Gap between the filled part and the track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressbar.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design (the default); set `false` for the newer look with a track gap and an end dot. iOS and macOS ignore it.

progressring.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.stroke_cap: Shape of the ring's line ends: `"butt"`, `"round"` or `"square"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the ring's track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
progressring.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for a spinning indicator.
progressring.progress: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0, the iOS name for `value`; when both are set, `progress` wins.
progressring.bgcolor: Color of the ring's track. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_width: Thickness of the ring, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_align: Where the stroke sits on the ring's path: `-1.0` inside, `0.0` centered, `1.0` outside (default: centered, or inside with `year_2023: false`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.size_constraints: Size limits of the ring, for example `{ min_width: 48, min_height: 48 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it; size the iOS indicator with `radius`.
progressring.padding: Space around the ring. iOS and macOS ignore it.

reorderablelistview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels.

responsiverow.columns: Number of virtual columns the row is divided into (default 12); `col` spans count in these.

searchbar.shrink_wrap: Sizes the search view to its suggestions.

semantics.header: Marks the content as a heading for screen readers.
semantics.expanded: Tells screen readers whether the content is expanded.
semantics.on_tap_hint_text: What screen readers say the tap action does, for example "Open".
semantics.on_long_press_hint_text: What screen readers say the long-press action does.
semantics.hint_text: What screen readers say acting on the control does, for example "Opens the message".
semantics.focus: Tells screen readers whether the control has input focus.
semantics.textfield: Tells screen readers that the content is a text field.
semantics.identifier: An identifier for UI tests and platform accessibility tools; screen readers do not announce it.

snackbar.action: The action button: a string label, whose button fires the snack bar's `on_action`, or a `snack_bar_action`, whose own `on_click` fires.
snackbar.duration: How long the snack bar stays visible, in milliseconds (default 4000).
snackbar.content: The message, usually a `text`; required (the first positional argument).
snackbar.persist: Keeps the snack bar open after `duration` until the user taps its action or close icon. On Android, web, Windows and Linux a snack bar with an `action` persists unless you pass `false`; on iOS and macOS it closes after `duration` unless you pass `true`.
snackbar.show_close_icon: Shows a close (x) button that dismisses the snack bar.
snackbar.bgcolor: Background color. On iOS and macOS the default is the system gray.
snackbar.padding: Padding inside the snack bar. On iOS and macOS the default is 16 on the left, 8 on the right and 10 above and below.
snackbar.margin: Space around a `"floating"` snack bar; ignored when `width` is set. On iOS and macOS it is the space around the bar (default 12 at the sides and bottom).
snackbar.width: Width of a `"floating"` snack bar. On iOS and macOS it sets the bar's width.
snackbar.behavior: `"fixed"` (default) spans the bottom edge of the screen; `"floating"` floats above it, and only then are `margin` and `width` used. iOS and macOS ignore it: their snack bar always floats near the bottom.
snackbar.action_overflow_threshold: Fraction of the snack bar's width, from 0.0 to 1.0, that the action may take before it moves below the message (default 0.25). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the snack bar, for example `"down"` (the default) or `"horizontal"`. iOS and macOS ignore it: the bar cannot be swiped away there.
snackbar.close_icon_color: Color of the close button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.clip_behavior: How the snack bar clips its content (default `"hardEdge"`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.elevation: Shadow depth of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.shape: Shape of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.on_visible: Fired when the snack bar appears.
snackbar.on_dismiss: Fired when the snack bar closes on its own: its time ran out, or the user swiped it away or tapped its action or close icon. Its `open` is `false` again.

snackbaraction.label: Text of the button; required (the first positional argument).
snackbaraction.text_color: Color of the label. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.bgcolor: Background color of the button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_text_color: Color of the label once the button has been pressed: an action works only once. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_bgcolor: Background color once the button has been pressed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled: Disables the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
snackbaraction.on_click: Fired when the user taps the button. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the snack bar then closes; on iOS and macOS it stays until its time runs out.

spinkit.variant: The indicator style; set it with the variant keyword you pass to `spinkit`, such as `three_bounce:`.
spinkit.size: Size of the indicator, in logical pixels (default 50).
spinkit.duration: Length of one animation cycle, in milliseconds.
spinkit.line_width: Line thickness of the `ring` and `dual_ring` variants (default 7) and of `spinning_lines` (default 2), in logical pixels.
spinkit.border_width: Border thickness of the `ripple` variant, in logical pixels (default 6).

table.rows: The `table_row` rows; the first positional argument, `rows:` or a block sets them.
table.border_color: Color of the table's lines; nothing is drawn without it.
table.border_width: Width of the lines, in logical pixels (default 1).
table.border_radius: Corner radius of the outer border.

tablerow.controls: The row's cells; the first positional argument, `controls:` or a block sets them. A hidden cell keeps its column.

contextmenu.open: On iOS and macOS the menu cannot be opened from code; it opens only from the user's long press.

events.on_reading: Fired with each reading: `event.data` is `{ x: ..., y: ..., z: ..., timestamp: ... }` (Symbol keys), the acceleration along each axis in m/s², gravity included, and the reading time as an ISO 8601 String.
events.on_error: Fired when the sensor stream fails: `event.data[:message]` is the client's message.

properties.configuration: Default recording settings, a Hash that `start_recording` sends when you pass no `configuration:`. Keys: `encoder` (default `"wav"`), `bit_rate` (128000), `sample_rate` (44100), `channels` (2), `auto_gain`, `cancel_echo` and `suppress_noise` (all false), `device` (`{ id:, label: }` from `get_input_devices`), `android_configuration` (`audio_source`, `manage_bluetooth`, `mute_audio`, `use_legacy`) and `ios_configuration` (`manage_audio_session`, `options`). Write encoder names as the client spells them, such as `"aacLc"`, `"opus"`, `"flac"`, `"wav"` or `"pcm16bits"`: the 0.0.23 client does not read `"aac_lc"` and records WAV instead. On `main` the client also reads `"aac_lc"`, and `device` also takes the id alone, a key of the `get_input_devices` Hash. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

events.on_state_change: Fired when recording starts, pauses or stops: `event.data` (also `event.state`) is `"recording"`, `"paused"` or `"stopped"`.
events.on_stream: Accepted, but no client sends it: recordings go to the `output_path` file.
events.on_upload: Accepted, but no client sends it, and `start_recording` ignores `upload:`.

methods.has_permission: Asks for microphone access the first time, then reports it. `on_result` receives `true` or `false`.
methods.start_recording: Starts recording to `output_path`, a writable file path on the device (build one from `page.get_application_documents_directory`). The web ignores the path. `configuration:` replaces the service's `configuration` for this recording. `on_result` receives `true` when recording started, or `false` without microphone access or, outside the web, without an `output_path`. `upload:` is ignored.
methods.stop_recording: Stops recording. `on_result` receives the recording's path, a blob URL on the web.
methods.pause_recording: Pauses the recording in progress. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.cancel_recording: Stops recording and deletes the file. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.is_recording: `on_result` receives `true` while a recording is running, paused or not.
methods.is_paused: `on_result` receives `true` while the recording is paused.
methods.is_supported_encoder: Checks one encoder name, such as `"opus"`. `on_result` receives `true` or `false`. With 0.0.23 it receives `nil` for a name the client does not know; on `main` such a name, or none, arrives as the error. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
methods.get_input_devices: Lists the microphones. `on_result` receives a Hash of device id => label.

events.on_reading: Fired with each reading: `event.data` is `{ pressure: ..., timestamp: ... }` (Symbol keys), the air pressure in hectopascals and the reading time as an ISO 8601 String.
events.on_error: Fired when the sensor stream fails: `event.data[:message]` is the client's message.

events.on_state_change: Fired when the charging state changes: `event.data[:state]` (also `event.state`) is `"charging"`, `"discharging"`, `"full"`, `"connectedNotCharging"` or `"unknown"`.

methods.get_battery_level: `on_result` receives the charge as an Integer percentage from 0 to 100, or `nil` when the device cannot report it.
methods.is_in_battery_save_mode: `on_result` receives `true` while the device is in battery-save (low power) mode.

methods.disable: Turns the browser's own right-click menu off, so the app's context menus can open. Only browsers have this menu: other clients answer with an error. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.enable: Turns the browser's right-click menu back on. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.disabled: Whether this service last sent `disable` (`false` until then). It is Ruby-side state, set when the call is sent, not read from the browser.

properties.preview_enabled: Shows the live preview when true (the default). Set false to hide it while the camera keeps running.

events.on_state_change: Fired when the camera's state changes: `event.data` is a Hash with these Symbol keys, read as `event.data[:is_initialized]`: `is_initialized`, `is_recording_video`, `is_recording_paused`, `is_taking_picture`, `is_streaming_images`, `is_preview_paused`, `flash_mode`, `exposure_mode`, `focus_mode`, `device_orientation`, `preview_size` (`width`, `height`), `aspect_ratio`, `has_error`, `error_description`, `description` (the camera) and the orientation-lock fields.
events.on_stream_image: Fired for each frame while `start_image_stream` runs: `event.data` has the Symbol keys `width`, `height`, `format` (the camera's format group), `encoded_format` (`"jpeg"`), `bytes` (the frame as a JPEG binary String) and the sensor's `lens_aperture`, `sensor_exposure_time` and `sensor_sensitivity`. A frame that arrives while the previous one is still being encoded is dropped.
events.on_error: Accepted, but the camera never sends it: failures arrive as the `error` of each method's `on_result`.

methods.get_available_cameras: `on_result` receives an Array of camera descriptions, Hashes with the String keys `"name"`, `"lens_direction"` (`"front"`, `"back"` or `"external"`), `"sensor_orientation"` and `"lens_type"`. Pass one to `initialize_camera`.
methods.initialize_camera: Opens a camera: `description` is a Hash from `get_available_cameras`, and `resolution_preset` is `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"veryHigh"`, `"ultraHigh"` or `"max"`. Options: `enable_audio:` (default true), `fps:`, `video_bitrate:`, `audio_bitrate:` and `image_format_group:` (`"jpeg"`, `"yuv420"`, `"bgra8888"` or `"nv21"`). Every other method needs it first. `on_result` receives `nil`; read the new state from `on_state_change`.
methods.take_picture: `on_result` receives the picture as a binary String.
methods.prepare_for_video_recording: Prepares the platform for recording, which shortens the delay before `start_video_recording` on iOS. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.resume_video_recording: Resumes a paused video recording. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.stop_video_recording: Stops recording. `on_result` receives the video as a binary String.
methods.supports_image_streaming: `on_result` receives `true` when this camera can stream frames.
methods.lock_capture_orientation: Locks the capture orientation to `"portraitUp"`, `"portraitDown"`, `"landscapeLeft"` or `"landscapeRight"`, or to the current device orientation when you pass nothing. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.unlock_capture_orientation: Lets the capture orientation follow the device again. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_description: Switches to another camera description from `get_available_cameras`. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_focus_mode: Sets the focus mode: `"auto"` or `"locked"`. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_focus_point: Focuses on a point, `{ x:, y: }` with values from 0.0 to 1.0 across the preview, or `nil` to reset. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_exposure_mode: Sets the exposure mode: `"auto"` or `"locked"`. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_exposure_point: Meters exposure at a point, `{ x:, y: }` with values from 0.0 to 1.0, or `nil` to reset. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_exposure_offset: Sets the exposure offset in EV, between `get_min_exposure_offset` and `get_max_exposure_offset`. `on_result` receives the offset the camera applied.
methods.get_exposure_offset_step_size: `on_result` receives the smallest exposure offset step, in EV.
methods.get_min_exposure_offset: `on_result` receives the lowest exposure offset, in EV.
methods.get_max_exposure_offset: `on_result` receives the highest exposure offset, in EV.
methods.set_zoom_level: Sets the zoom, between `get_min_zoom_level` and `get_max_zoom_level`. `on_result` receives `nil`.

methods.set: Copies the value, converted with `to_s`, to the clipboard as text. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.get: `on_result` receives the clipboard's text, or `nil` when it holds no text.
methods.set_image: Copies an image to the clipboard: the encoded image (for example PNG) as a binary String or an Array of byte Integers. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.get_image: `on_result` receives the clipboard's image as a binary String, or `nil`.
methods.set_files: Puts files on the clipboard by path (each value converted with `to_s`). `on_result` receives `true` when the clipboard accepted them.
methods.get_files: `on_result` receives the paths of the files on the clipboard, an Array of Strings.

events.on_change: Fired when the network connection changes: `event.data[:connectivity]` lists the active connection types, such as `["wifi"]` or `["none"]`.

methods.get_connectivity: `on_result` receives the active connection types, an Array of `"wifi"`, `"mobile"`, `"ethernet"`, `"vpn"`, `"bluetooth"`, `"satellite"`, `"other"` or `"none"` when offline.

events.on_result: Accepted, but no client sends it: each method returns its answer to its own `on_result:` callback.
events.on_upload: Fired as `upload` sends a file: `event.data` has `:file_name`, `:progress` (from 0.0 to 1.0, sent about every 10%) and `:error` (the failure message, or `nil`).

methods.pick_files: Opens the file picker. Options: `dialog_title:`, `initial_directory:`, `file_type:` (`"any"`, `"media"`, `"image"`, `"video"`, `"audio"` or `"custom"`; `allowed_extensions:` such as `["pdf"]` switches to `"custom"`), `allow_multiple:` and `with_data:`. `on_result` receives an Array of Hashes with `"id"`, `"name"`, `"path"` (`nil` on the web), `"size"` in bytes and `"bytes"` (only with `with_data: true`), or `[]` when the user cancels. The service waits `timeout:` seconds for the user, 10 by default; pass a longer one, or call `page.pick_files`, which has none.
methods.save_file: Opens a save dialog. Takes the `pick_files` options plus `file_name:` and `src_bytes:` (the contents, a binary String or an Array of byte Integers). Android, iOS and the web need `src_bytes:` and save it; the web also needs `file_name:`. `on_result` receives the chosen path, or `nil` when the user cancels.
methods.get_directory_path: Lets the user pick a folder (`dialog_title:`, `initial_directory:`). `on_result` receives its path, or `nil` when the user cancels. The web raises an error.
methods.upload: Uploads files picked with this service's last `pick_files` call. `files` is an Array of Hashes with `name:` (or the picked `id:`), `upload_url:`, the absolute URL of an endpoint your app provides, which receives the raw file body, and `method:` such as `"PUT"`. `on_result` receives `nil` at once; follow progress with `on_upload`. Pick with `with_data: false` (the default): the upload reads the file's stream.

events.on_error: Accepted, but the flashlight never sends it: failures arrive as the `error` of each method's `on_result`.

methods.is_available: `on_result` receives `true` when the device has a torch. Android and iOS only: other clients answer with an error.
methods.on: Turns the torch on. `on_result` receives `nil`. Android and iOS only.
methods.off: Turns the torch off. `on_result` receives `nil`. Android and iOS only.

properties.configuration: Location settings for `on_position_change` (and the default for nothing else): `accuracy` (`"lowest"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"best"`, the default, or `"bestForNavigation"`), `distance_filter` (meters a device moves before the next update, default 0), `time_limit`, plus Android keys (`interval_duration`, `foreground_notification_*`) and Apple keys (`activity_type`, `pause_location_updates_automatically`, `show_background_location_indicator`, `allow_background_location_updates`). Changing it restarts the position stream.

events.on_position_change: Fired with each new position while the handler is set: `event.data[:position]` is a position Hash with Symbol keys, such as `event.data[:position][:latitude]`, and the fields of `get_current_position`.
events.on_error: Fired when the position stream or `get_current_position` fails: `event.data` is the client's message.

methods.request_permission: Shows the location permission prompt when the user has not answered yet. `on_result` receives the status: `"denied"`, `"deniedForever"`, `"whileInUse"`, `"always"` or `"unableToDetermine"`.
methods.get_permission_status: `on_result` receives the location permission status, as for `request_permission`, without prompting.
methods.is_location_service_enabled: `on_result` receives `true` when the device's location services are on.
methods.get_current_position: Reads the position once, with `configuration:` settings (see the property). `on_result` receives a Hash with String keys, such as `position["latitude"]`: `latitude`, `longitude`, `accuracy` (meters), `altitude`, `altitude_accuracy`, `heading`, `heading_accuracy`, `speed` (m/s), `speed_accuracy`, `floor`, `mocked` and `timestamp` (an ISO 8601 String). A failure fires `on_error`. With 0.0.23, `on_result` then receives `nil` and no error; on `main` it receives the error too. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
methods.get_last_known_position: `on_result` receives the last cached position Hash, or `nil`. The web answers `nil`.
methods.distance_between: Computes the distance between two latitude/longitude pairs on the client. `on_result` receives meters as a Float.
methods.open_app_settings: Opens the app's settings page so the user can change the permission. `on_result` receives `true` when it opened. The web answers `nil`.
methods.open_location_settings: Opens the device's location settings. `on_result` receives `true` when they opened. The web answers `nil`.

events.on_reading: Fired with each reading: `event.data` is `{ x: ..., y: ..., z: ..., timestamp: ... }` (Symbol keys), the rotation rate around each axis in rad/s, and the reading time as an ISO 8601 String.
events.on_error: Fired when the sensor stream fails: `event.data[:message]` is the client's message.

methods.heavy_impact: Plays a heavy impact. `on_result` receives `nil`. Devices and browsers without haptics do nothing.
methods.selection_click: Plays the tick used when a selection changes. `on_result` receives `nil`.

methods.authenticate: Shows the system prompt with `localized_reason:`. `biometric_only: true` refuses the device PIN, pattern or passcode; `sensitive_transaction:` (default true) and `persist_across_backgrounding:` follow the platform plugin, and `android_messages:`, `ios_messages:` and `macos_messages:` change the prompt's texts. `on_result` receives `true` on success and `false` when the user failed the challenge; cancellation, lockout and missing hardware arrive as the error (read it with `Ruflet::LocalAuthError.from_error`). Waits 60 seconds by default.
methods.authenticate_sync: `authenticate` that waits for the answer and returns it. It raises Ruflet::LocalAuthError for a client error and Timeout::Error after `timeout`. Do not call it inside an event handler: handlers run on the thread that delivers the answer.
methods.can_check_biometrics: `on_result` receives `true` when the device has biometric hardware.
methods.can_check_biometrics_sync: `can_check_biometrics` that waits and returns the answer.
methods.is_device_supported: `on_result` receives `true` when the device can authenticate with biometrics or its credential.
methods.is_device_supported_sync: `is_device_supported` that waits and returns the answer.
methods.get_available_biometrics: `on_result` receives the enrolled biometrics: an Array of `"face"`, `"fingerprint"`, `"iris"`, `"strong"` or `"weak"`.
methods.get_available_biometrics_sync: `get_available_biometrics` that waits and returns the answer.
methods.stop_authentication: Cancels a prompt in progress (Android). `on_result` receives `true` when one was cancelled.
methods.stop_authentication_sync: `stop_authentication` that waits and returns the answer.

events.on_reading: Fired with each reading: `event.data` is `{ x: ..., y: ..., z: ..., timestamp: ... }` (Symbol keys), the magnetic field along each axis in microteslas, and the reading time as an ISO 8601 String.
events.on_error: Fired when the sensor stream fails: `event.data[:message]` is the client's message.

methods.request: Asks for one permission, named as the client spells it, case-insensitive: for example `"camera"`, `"microphone"`, `"location"`, `"locationWhenInUse"`, `"locationAlways"`, `"photos"`, `"contacts"`, `"notification"`, `"bluetooth"` or `"storage"`. `on_result` receives the status: `"granted"`, `"denied"`, `"permanentlyDenied"`, `"restricted"`, `"limited"` or `"provisional"`, or `nil` for an unknown name. The app's `services.yaml` must declare the matching protected access.
methods.get_status: Reads one permission's status without prompting. `on_result` receives a status as for `request`, or `nil` for an unknown name.
methods.open_app_settings: Opens the app's settings page. `on_result` receives `true` when it opened.

events.on_system_screen_brightness_change: Fired when the system brightness changes: `event.data[:brightness]` is the new level from 0.0 to 1.0. The web never sends it.
events.on_application_screen_brightness_change: Fired when the app's brightness changes: `event.data[:brightness]` is the new level from 0.0 to 1.0. The web never sends it.

methods.get_system_screen_brightness: `on_result` receives the system brightness from 0.0 to 1.0. The web answers `nil` to every method of this service.
methods.can_change_system_screen_brightness: `on_result` receives `true` when the app may change the system brightness.
methods.set_system_screen_brightness: Sets the system brightness, from 0.0 to 1.0. On this service object the call fails: it sends the level under a name the client does not read. Call it on the `page.screen_brightness` proxy instead.
methods.get_application_screen_brightness: `on_result` receives the brightness the app currently uses, from 0.0 to 1.0.
methods.set_application_screen_brightness: Sets the brightness while the app is in front, from 0.0 to 1.0. On this service object the call fails: it sends the level under a name the client does not read. Call it on the `page.screen_brightness` proxy instead.
methods.reset_application_screen_brightness: Returns the app to the system brightness. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.set_animate: Turns brightness animation on or off. On this service object the call fails, as for the brightness setters; call it on the `page.screen_brightness` proxy.
methods.is_auto_reset: `on_result` receives `true` when the app brightness resets when the app leaves the foreground.
methods.set_auto_reset: Turns the automatic reset on or off. On this service object the call fails, as for the brightness setters; call it on the `page.screen_brightness` proxy.

proxy_methods.set_system_screen_brightness: Sets the system brightness, from 0.0 to 1.0, where `can_change_system_screen_brightness` allows it. `on_result` receives `nil`.
proxy_methods.set_application_screen_brightness: Sets the brightness while the app is in front, from 0.0 to 1.0. `on_result` receives `nil`.
proxy_methods.set_animate: Turns brightness animation on or off. `on_result` receives `nil`.
proxy_methods.set_auto_reset: Turns the automatic reset on or off. `on_result` receives `nil`.

properties.ios_options: iOS keychain settings: `accessibility` (default `"unlocked"`; also `"passcode"`, `"unlocked_this_device"`, `"first_unlock"` and `"first_unlock_this_device"`), `account_name`, `group_id`, `synchronizable` (false), `label`, `description`, `comment`, `access_control_flags` and the other keychain attributes.
properties.macos_options: macOS keychain settings: the `ios_options` keys plus `uses_data_protection_keychain` (default true).

events.on_change: Fired on iOS and macOS when protected data becomes available or unavailable, for example when the device locks: `event.data[:available]` is `true` or `false`.

methods.set: Stores `value` under `key`. Pass a String: the 0.0.23 client rejects other values. Options for one call: `android:`, `ios:`, `macos:`, `web:` and `windows:` (Hashes like the matching `*_options`), `timeout:` and `on_result:`, which receives `nil`.
methods.get: `on_result` receives the String stored under `key`, or `nil`. Takes the same per-call options as `set`.
methods.get_all: `on_result` receives every stored key and value as a Hash.
methods.clear: Deletes every value this app stored. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.get_availability: `on_result` receives `true` when protected data can be read now (iOS and macOS); other platforms answer `nil`.

methods.announce_message: Asks the screen reader to read `message`. `rtl: true` reads it right to left. The clients always announce politely, whatever `assertiveness:` says. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.get_accessibility_features: `on_result` receives the accessibility settings in use, a Hash of `true`/`false` values: `accessible_navigation`, `bold_text`, `disable_animations`, `high_contrast`, `invert_colors`, `reduce_motion`, `on_off_switch_labels` and `supports_announcements`.

properties.shake_slop_time_ms: Milliseconds after a shake during which further movement is ignored (default 500).
properties.shake_count_reset_time_ms: Milliseconds without a shake after which the count starts again (default 3000).
properties.shake_threshold_gravity: Acceleration, in multiples of gravity, a movement must exceed to count as a shake (default 2.7).

events.on_shake: Fired when the device was shaken `minimum_shake_count` times. `event.data` is `nil`.

methods.share_text: Opens the share sheet for `text`, with `title:` and `subject:` (used by email targets). `preview_thumbnail:` takes a file Hash (see `share_files`), `share_position_origin:` the `{ x:, y:, width:, height: }` area an iPad popover points to, and `excluded_cupertino_activities:` the iOS activities to hide. On the web, `download_fallback_enabled:` and `mail_to_fallback_enabled:` (both true) allow the fallbacks when the browser cannot share. `on_result` receives `{"status" => "success" | "dismissed" | "unavailable", "raw" => ...}`.
methods.share_uri: Opens the share sheet for a link. Takes `share_position_origin:` and `excluded_cupertino_activities:`. `on_result` receives the status Hash, as for `share_text`.
methods.share_files: Shares files, each a Hash with `path:` or `data:` (a binary String or an Array of byte Integers), plus optional `name:` and `mime_type:`. Takes the `share_text` options. `page.share_files` also accepts plain path Strings; the service object does not. `on_result` receives the status Hash, as for `share_text`.

methods.set: Stores `value` under `key`. Pass a String: the 0.0.23 client rejects other values. `on_result` receives `true` when it was saved.
methods.get: `on_result` receives the String stored under `key`, or `nil`.
methods.get_keys: `on_result` receives the stored keys that start with `key_prefix`, an Array of Strings. Pass `""` for every key.
methods.remove: Deletes `key`. `on_result` receives `true` when it was removed.

methods.get_application_documents_directory: `on_result` receives the directory for the user's documents, a path String. The web answers `nil` to every method of this service.
methods.get_application_support_directory: `on_result` receives the directory for app files the user does not see.
methods.get_temporary_directory: `on_result` receives a temporary directory the system may clear.
methods.get_downloads_directory: `on_result` receives the downloads directory, or `nil` where the platform has none.
methods.get_library_directory: `on_result` receives the Library directory on iOS and macOS, and `nil` elsewhere.
methods.get_external_storage_directory: `on_result` receives the app's directory on external storage on Android, and `nil` elsewhere.
methods.get_external_storage_directories: `on_result` receives an Array of the app's external storage directories on Android, and `nil` elsewhere.
methods.get_external_cache_directories: `on_result` receives an Array of the app's external cache directories on Android, and `nil` elsewhere.
methods.get_console_log_filename: `on_result` receives the path of `console.log` in the app's cache directory.

methods.launch_url: Opens `url`. `mode:` is `"platformDefault"` (the default), `"inAppWebView"`, `"inAppBrowserView"`, `"externalApplication"` or `"externalNonBrowserApplication"`; `web_view_configuration:` takes `enable_javascript`, `enable_dom_storage` and `headers`, `browser_configuration:` takes `show_title`, and `web_only_window_name:` names the browser tab, such as `"_blank"`. `on_result` receives `nil`. Some failures arrive as the error, but the client does not check whether the URL opened, so others leave both `nil`. Call `can_launch_url` first to find out whether an app can open it.
methods.can_launch_url: `on_result` receives `true` when an app can open `url`.
methods.close_in_app_web_view: Closes a page opened with `mode: "inAppWebView"`. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.open_window: Opens `url` in a browser popup window, `width:` by `height:` pixels (default 1200 by 800). Only the web opens one; other clients do nothing. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.supports_launch_mode: `on_result` receives `true` when the platform supports the launch `mode`.
methods.supports_close_for_launch_mode: `on_result` receives `true` when a page opened with `mode` can be closed with `close_in_app_web_view`.

events.on_reading: Fired with each reading: `event.data` is `{ x: ..., y: ..., z: ..., timestamp: ... }` (Symbol keys), the acceleration along each axis in m/s² without gravity, and the reading time in microseconds since the Unix epoch.
events.on_error: Fired when the sensor stream fails: `event.data[:message]` is the client's message.

methods.enable: Keeps the screen on while the app is open. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.disable: Lets the screen turn off again. `on_result` receives `nil`.
methods.is_enabled: `on_result` receives `true` while the screen is kept on.

page.pick_files: Same as the service's `pick_files`, without a timeout unless you pass one.
page.can_launch_url: Sends the check but takes no `on_result:`, so the answer is lost. Use `page.url_launcher.can_launch_url(url, on_result: ...)` to read it.
